reasons: A failed fetch is cached as empty, which hides a working feed for 15 minutes after one error.
Feed parsing uses text patterns rather than a proper XML parser.
The industry is read through a type cast, which suggests the source type may not declare that field.

terms.meaning: a standard feed format that lists recent articles from a website.
another feed format, read here as a fallback.
a tagged text format that feeds are written in.
a wrapper that marks text as raw content, so special characters inside are kept.
a saved copy kept for a while so it does not have to be fetched again.
a limit on how long to wait before giving up.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and time limits
sections.what: Brings in the search and source types and sets the 10-second feed timeout and 15-minute cache length.
sections.why: Likely reason: a slow feed must not hold up the whole search, and feeds should not be refetched constantly.

sections.name: CachedFeed
sections.title: Cached feed shape
sections.what: Describes a saved feed: its articles and the time it was fetched.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to tell whether the saved copy is still fresh.

sections.name: RSSItem, feedCache
sections.title: Article shape and feed store
sections.what: Describes one article read from a feed, and creates the in-memory store that keeps feeds for reuse, keyed by feed address.
sections.why: Likely reason: keying by address means each feed is fetched and cached separately.
sections.watch_out: The store lives only in memory and grows with each new feed address.

sections.name: tierToScore
sections.title: Tier to trust score
sections.what: Converts a source tier from 1 to 5 into a trust score from 100 down to 20. Any other tier gets 30.
sections.why: Likely reason: more trusted tiers get higher scores, and unknown tiers sit in the middle.
sections.watch_out: The same mapping is repeated in router.ts, so changing one without the other makes scores disagree.

sections.name: keywordMatch
sections.title: Word match check
sections.what: Returns true when any search word longer than two letters appears in the given text, ignoring case.
sections.why: Likely reason: skips short filler words that would match almost anything.

sections.name: parseFeed
sections.title: Fetching one feed
sections.what: Downloads a feed address with a 10-second timeout and a named user agent, then reads its articles. A failed download or an error reply returns an empty list.
sections.why: Likely reason: one broken feed should not stop the rest of the search.
sections.watch_out: Failures return an empty list rather than an error, so a broken feed looks the same as a quiet one.

sections.name: parseXml
sections.title: Reading feed text
sections.what: Pulls articles out of the feed text. It reads standard feed items first, and only tries the Atom style if none are found.
sections.why: Likely reason: supports both common feed styles with one function.
sections.watch_out: Pattern-based reading can miss articles with unusual tag layouts.

sections.name: extractTag
sections.title: Finding one tag's text
sections.what: Returns the trimmed text inside the first matching tag, or nothing if the tag is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: a small helper keeps the reader short.
sections.watch_out: Only the first occurrence of each tag is read.

sections.name: cleanCdata
sections.title: Removing wrapper text
sections.what: Strips the raw-content wrapper so only the text inside remains.
sections.why: Likely reason: many feeds wrap titles and summaries in this wrapper.

sections.name: RSSProvider (part 1)
sections.title: Provider entry point, part 1
sections.what: Loads enabled RSS sources, narrows them to the requested industry when one is given, then fetches or reuses each feed in parallel. A feed whose fetch fails contributes nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps feeds curated per industry, so unrelated feeds do not answer.
sections.watch_out: Industry narrowing relies on a field the source type may not declare.

sections.name: RSSProvider: for
sections.title: Provider entry point, part 2
sections.what: Keeps articles whose title or summary matches the search words, gives each one a trust score from its source tier, sorts by publish date with newest first, and returns the requested number.
sections.why: Likely reason: newest first puts recent news ahead of older items.
sections.watch_out: Articles with no date sort to the bottom, so they can fall off the list when the limit is small.

summary: Reads the curated news feeds for an industry and returns articles whose title or summary mention the search words, newest first.
purpose: Gives search results from trusted industry news feeds, which need no API key.
why: Likely reason: feed lists are curated per industry. The comment says unrelated articles appeared in results before this was added.
how: Loads enabled RSS sources, keeps only those for the requested industry, and fetches each feed in parallel with a 10-second limit. Each feed is cached for 15 minutes. It reads each article from the feed text, keeps articles where a search word longer than two letters appears in the title or summary, gives each one a trust score from its source tier, sorts newest first, and returns the requested number.
inputs: Search text, result limit, an optional industry, and a loader for enabled sources. Each source gives a web address, a tier, an industry, and a type.
outputs: A list of search results with address, title, summary text, source name rss, trust score, and published date when present.
risks: A failed fetch returns an empty list which is then cached for 15 minutes, so one error hides that feed for a while. Feed contents are read with text patterns rather than a real XML reader, so unusual feeds may be misread.
debug: If a feed shows no results, check its address and whether the fetch timed out. A log line reports how many feeds are in scope for the industry. If results come from the wrong industry, check each source's industry value. The cache lives in memory, so a restart clears it.
